objectives: Run a transfer of OOD shares from the first request to the filing in the Commercial Register.
Prepare the certification of a manager's specimen signature and consent.
Certify protocols of general meetings and sole-owner decisions in the right form.
Apply the anti-money laundering checks to company clients.

cards.front: Partner A sells her share to partner B. Must the general meeting consent?
cards.back: **No**: a transfer between partners is free ([[tz:129:1]]). The contract still needs signatures and content certified at the same time ([[tz:129:2|Art. 129(2)]]).

cards.front: What majority admits a new partner in an OOD?
cards.back: More than **three quarters** of the capital, unless the articles require more ([[tz:137:3]]).

cards.front: What declaration accompanies a share transfer to a third person?
cards.back: A declaration by the manager and the transferor that there are **no unpaid wages**, compensations or social contributions of the workers ([[tz:129:2]]).

cards.front: In how many copies is a share transfer contract certified?
cards.back: **Two or more** identical copies; one stays with the notary ([[gpk:590:4]]).

cards.front: What is the deadline to file a change in the Commercial Register?
What does a new manager present to the register?
cards.back: A notarially certified **consent with a specimen signature** ([[tz:141:3]]).

cards.front: Which OOD decisions need protocols with signatures and content certified?
cards.back: Admission and expulsion of partners and consent to a transfer; capital changes; election of a manager; real estate ([[tz:137:4]]).

cards.front: The articles of an OOD provide written form for decisions. Is a protocol with simple signatures enough to elect a manager?
cards.back: **Yes**: the notarial form of [[tz:137:4]] applies unless the articles provide written form.
The fee for the **content** that the Commerce Act or the Special Pledges Act requires to be certified with the signatures. The provision does not name the fee for the signatures.

cards.front: A new manager was entered on 1 March. On 10 March a supplier contracted with the old manager, unaware of the change. Is the supplier bound by the entry?
cards.back: An entered fact is deemed known from the entry, but for **15 days** it cannot be opposed to a third person who proves that it was impossible to know it ([[ztr:7:1]]).

cards.front: Where is a special pledge over company shares entered?
cards.back: In the **Central Register of Special Pledges** ([[zoz:2:1]]).

cards.front: How does the notary identify the beneficial owner of a company?
cards.back: From the register data; when they are insufficient or contradictory, a **declaration** by the representative ([[zmip:59:1]]).

quiz.question: An OOD has three partners. One sells her share to an outside investor. What is needed besides the contract?
options: A decision of the general meeting admitting the investor
A decision of the manager approving the new partner
A decision of the district court approving the transfer
A declaration of the workers that they agree to the transfer
quiz.explanation: [[tz:129:1]]: a transfer to a third person follows the rules for admitting a new partner: a decision of the general meeting ([[tz:137:1:2|Art. 137(1) item 2]]) by more than three quarters of the capital ([[tz:137:3|Art. 137(3)]]), in a protocol with signatures and content certified at the same time, unless the articles provide written form ([[tz:137:4|Art. 137(4)]]).

quiz.question: What prevents the registration of a share transfer to a third person?
options: Unpaid wages or social contributions of the workers
A bank loan of the company that is not yet due
A lease of the office that runs for five more years
A pending lawsuit of the company with a supplier
quiz.explanation: [[tz:129:1]]: a transfer to a third person is possible only when there are no unpaid wages, compensations or mandatory social contributions of the workers, including those who left in the last three years; the manager and the transferor declare this ([[tz:129:2|Art. 129(2)]]). From 2 April 2027 the registration officer also checks it electronically at the NRA.

quiz.question: Within how many days must the company file the share transfer with the Commercial Register?
options: 7 days from the change
14 days from the change
1 month from the change
3 days from the change
quiz.explanation: [[ztr:6:2]]: a person who must file a fact for entry does so within 7 days of the fact, unless a law sets another term.

quiz.question: The general meeting elected a new manager in a protocol with simple signatures; the articles say nothing about form. What is the status of the election?
options: Null; the election needs certified signatures and content
Valid; the form of the protocol is free for an election
Voidable; a partner may challenge it within 14 days of the meeting
Valid only after the entry in the Commercial Register
quiz.explanation: [[tz:137:4]]: the election of a manager ([[tz:137:1:5|Art. 137(1) item 5]], first part) is recorded in a protocol with signatures and content certified at the same time, unless the articles provide written form; [[tz:137:5|Art. 137(5)]]: a decision taken in breach of that form is null. The entry does not heal a null decision.

quiz.question: What does a manager sign at the notary for the Commercial Register?
options: A consent with a specimen signature, with the signature certified
A declaration of his income, with the signature certified
A notarial deed of his appointment, before two witnesses and the partners
A protocol of the general meeting, with his signature only
quiz.explanation: [[tz:141:3]]: the name of the manager is entered in the Commercial Register; the manager presents a notarially certified consent with a specimen signature. The election itself is in the protocol of the general meeting ([[tz:137:4|Art. 137(4)]]).

quiz.question: A sole trader transfers his business to his new EOOD. What form does the contract need?
options: Written, with signatures and content certified at the same time
A notarial deed, entered in the property register
Simple written form, filed with the Commercial Register within 7 days
Written form with the signatures certified only
quiz.explanation: [[tz:15:1]]: an enterprise is transferred by a written contract with signatures and content certified at the same time; the transfer is entered in the Commercial Register in the files of both parties ([[tz:16:1|Art. 16(1)]]), and in the registry office when real estate is included ([[tz:16:5|Art. 16(5)]]).

quiz.question: A share transfer contract needs signature and content certified at the same time. What does Art. 90(2) ЗННД say about its fee?
options: The content costs an ordinary fee, not a fee on the price
The content costs item 8 on the price of the shares
The content costs item 9 on the registered capital of the company
The certification costs nothing for a company
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:90:2]]: when the Commerce Act requires the content to be certified together with the signatures, an ordinary fee is due for the content. Items 8 and 9 are fees on a material interest, and no certification is free for a company. The provision does not name the fee for the signatures (chapter 28).

quiz.question: The register shows a beneficial owner, but the company says the owner changed last month. What does the notary do?
options: Asks for a declaration by the legal representative, with documents
Relies on the register; it is the only source the law allows
Refuses the act until the company corrects the register and the data
Relies on the oral statement of the client, noted in the file
quiz.explanation: [[zmip:59:1]]: the beneficial owner is identified from the register (item 1) and from documents (item 2); when the information is insufficient or contradictory, a declaration by the legal representative or agent is required (item 3).

quiz.question: May a mayor in a village certify the signatures on a share transfer?
options: No; mayors may not certify such signatures
Yes; mayors certify signatures like a notary
Yes, if the village has no notary and no court
Yes, with the consent of the Notary Chamber
quiz.explanation: [[znnd:83:2]]: the mayors and municipal officials of [[znnd:83:1|Art. 83(1)]] may not certify signatures on private documents in the cases of [[tz:15:1|Art. 15(1)]], [[tz:129:2|129(2)]] and [[tz:137:6|137(6) ТЗ]]: the transfer of an enterprise, the transfer of shares and the power to vote in a general meeting. The absence of a notary does not change this.

quiz.question: A company pledges its shares in a subsidiary to a bank. Where is the pledge entered?
options: In the Central Register of Special Pledges
In the property register at the registry office
In the notary's book of copies only
In the Commercial Register, in the file of the bank
quiz.explanation: [[zoz:2:1]]: a special pledge is created by its entry in the Central Register of Special Pledges on the basis of a pledge contract; the contract is in writing, in the cases provided by the law with notarially certified signatures ([[zoz:2:2|Art. 2(2)]]).

quiz.question: The articles of an OOD provide written form for decisions of the general meeting. The partners elect a manager in a protocol with simple signatures. Is the election valid?
options: Yes; the articles may replace the notarial form with written form
No; the election of a manager always needs certified signatures
No; the articles cannot change the form that the law prescribes for it
Yes, but only if the protocol is entered in the Chamber's system
quiz.explanation: [[tz:137:4]]: the protocol with signatures and content certified at the same time is required "unless the articles provide written form". With such a clause a protocol with simple signatures is valid; the Chamber's system receives only certified documents ([[n32:9а]]).

quiz.question: A share transfer contract was certified by a notary who did not enter it in the information system of the Chamber. What does the registration officer do?
options: Refuses the entry; the document must be in the information system
Enters the transfer; the entry in the system is the notary's duty only
Enters the transfer after a declaration of the manager about the contract
Sends the contract back to the notary for a second certification
quiz.explanation: [[ztr:21::9|Art. 21 item 9 ЗТРРЮЛНЦ]]: the registration officer checks that documents which the law requires with a certified signature, or signature and content, are entered in the information system of the Notary Chamber and match the entered data. The notary enters the extract under [[n32:9а::4|Art. 9а item 4 of Ordinance No. 32]]; the company asks the notary to do so.
